result: acted: A NEW MAC BRANCH, AND IT ANSWERS THE QUESTION THE CLOUD LANE COULD NOT. mac/intake-airllm appeared (8f322688, 17:29Z) — the first mac/* movement since 2026-09-14 19:25 — and it is the Mac lane having RUN AirLLM rather than read about it. Opened as DRAFT PR #801 per step 3, subscribed, reviewed against the standing checklist: one documentation line, no behaviour edits, nothing of the tool in the tree (scratch venv under $TMPDIR, no keys, no dependency), source read BEFORE running, and honest about what was not measured (the 70B itself, ~140 GB, and the offline re-run — named as not recomputed rather than estimated). No blocker; recommended landing. THE MEASUREMENT: TinyLlama-1.1B produced 20 tokens in 207.1s and again in 205.7s = 0.1 tok/s, while qwen3:8b under the Ollama already installed on that SAME Mac measures 12.7 tok/s — roughly 100x faster on a model about 7x larger. Peak footprint 2.44 GB for a 2.2 GB model, so the layer-streaming saved almost nothing because the model already fitted; Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct failed outright because the MLX backend cannot load a tied-embedding model, which covers the current small Llamas; temperature 0 output identical across both runs. The README is not wrong, it answers a different question: its 70B-on-4GB claim is about MEMORY and holds by construction, and the cost it omits is TIME, which scales with layer count and size, so a 70B on that hardware would be minutes per token. TWO LANES CONVERGED FROM OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS WITHOUT COORDINATING: the Mac measured HOW FAST and the cloud fenced WHERE IT MAY EVER LIVE (#800, scripts/check-decision-path-purity.mjs — 29 files, no network, no subprocess, no inference client, self-test 8/8, falsified by planting an OpenAI import in engine.ts). Both reached the same boundary sentence independently: never lib/*, /v1, connectors or proofs, golden rule 2. I UPDATED MY OWN PR RATHER THAN LEAVE A STALE CLAIM: #800's owner-gated backlog row said latency was the question only measurement could settle; it is settled, so the row now cites the figure and the redirect (a quantized model under the existing Ollama, not this). Leaving it open would have been a claim that lies. ONE CONFLICT FLAGGED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER: #800 and #801 both append to the tail of docs/agent/RESOURCE_INTAKE.md and will conflict textually; either order works, whichever lands second keeps BOTH rows, and the cloud lane does that resolution rather than leaving it to the Mac.
